title: Meta's Muse agent gains access to ad accounts and 15 business tools
source_used: PPC Land (fulltext fetched by main session)
key_facts: On 29 Sep 2026 Meta announced Muse for Small Business, a set of skills and connectors inside its Muse personal AI agent, which launched on 8 Sep 2026.
It adds connectors to 15 third-party tools, including Shopify, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Stripe and Canva, plus Facebook Pages, Instagram professional-account analytics and Meta ad accounts.
Meta says nothing publishes, sends or spends without the owner's approval.

It is offered in the US and Canada only; Meta says Muse is free for most uses and plans subscription tiers but gives no prices (PPC Land cites Digiday for $20 and $100 monthly tiers, which Meta has not confirmed).
Meta has not said whether access to an ad account is read-only or can change budgets, bids or creative, or how connector data is kept apart from its ad systems.
PPC Land notes Amazon blocked Muse from its store in the week to 27 Sep and that Meta's second-quarter 2026 revenue was $60.80 billion, more than 97 percent of it from ads.
Quantified outcome in the announcement: one grocery owner said Muse cut at least 15 minutes from payroll.
quote_evidence: Meta on September 29, 2026 extended Muse, the personal AI agent it released three weeks earlier, into a product for small businesses, adding connectors to 15 third-party tools including Shopify, Intuit QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Stripe and Canva.
The company says nothing publishes, sends or spends without the owner's approval.

The post gives no list of skills, no description of which actions each connector permits, and no indication of whether access to a Meta ad account is read-only or includes changes to budgets, bids or creative.
why_it_matters_hint: A Meta-built agent now sits inside Meta ad accounts next to a shop's store, accounting and customer data, while key limits are undefined.
notes: Older news re-dated: the announcement is from 29 Sep 2026 and our 10 Oct 2026 edition already carried the launch (Retail Dive as relayed by MLive, on Amazon asking to be removed). PPC Land's 11 Oct piece adds analysis, not a new event. Official Meta Newsroom post as read by PPC Land.
